name: Upsized EFI fuel plumbing: 3/8" NiCopp + -6AN PTFE, Trick Flow filter
model: TFS-23000 · Trick Flow TFX inline 40-micron filter, -6AN; 3/8" NiCopp hard line both ways, -6AN PTFE hose, Breeze Let-Lok hard-line-to-AN transitions, Lode Stone BilletWorks clamps, Loctite 567 on NPT
users: Papa (Terminator X, 347); Afdent11 (Sniper 2, BP 347) upsizing; Sea Hut went Aeromotive in-tank pump, regulator and EZ-Flo filter with soft lines
notes: The kit ships 5/16" supply and 1/4" return; Papa calls the return undersized for EFI and Holley asks for 3/8" both ways. Route tank → over the rear end → driver side of the tunnel → engine bay; the bigger filter mounts at the tunnel, not on the tank side the manual shows. NPT-to-AN adapters (Russell, Evil Energy) threaded only two turns into some filters: check NPT vs ORB ports before buying. Pressure-test PTFE hose (Fragola 900666 kit) before final assembly. The kit PTFE lines with AN ends are fine if you keep the stock sizes. Chris #566 gave up on stainless hard fuel line after a 1/16" pulley misalignment on his straightener ovaled the 3/8" tube, and ran SS-braided PTFE instead (NiCopp for the brakes).
popWhy: Papa, Afdent11, 95050JohnR; Sea Hut did the Aeromotive version

name: H3 LED bulbs for the FFR driving / fog lights

users: PNWTim #620 (fit confirmed, 0.9 A vs >12 A halogen); Papa ordered the same
notes: The glass lens does not come off. Remove the ground screw on the back of the housing and the bulb fixture comes out; feed the terminals through the rubber boot gently. Bulb must be shorter than ~2.125"; fan-cooled bulbs will not fit. The only halogens left on the car once the headlights and tails are LED.

name: Snakebite driver footbox extension (pedal room)
model: Snakebite Motorworks driver-side footbox extension, $106; passenger side $107; includes hardware and rivets

notes: The pedals sit left of the seat centerline in every coupe; edwardb and 8secDuster both call the offset a non-issue you adapt to, and 8secDuster says the real problem on a Gen 2 was clutch/brake pad spacing (his left foot caught the brake). users: Papa (hated the kit cable setup; Lokar on the coupe)

name: 1" wheel spacers for 315s on the IRS (frame rub)
model: Eibach Pro-Spacer 90.4.25.010.3, 25 mm (edwardb); or wheels with 5.46" backspacing instead of the FFR 6.46" (Papa)
users: edwardb #59 (315/30-18 Rival S, 1" spacer, -0.5 to -0.75° camber, 11k miles, no rub); Papa; Jphoenix notched the frame instead
src: Gen 3 IRS frame rub – Koni mount hole? (new forum 136432)
notes: 315s on the 18" Halibrands rub the frame behind the passenger seat on the IRS. The coupe body is wider than the roadster but the suspension is the same, which is why the spacer exists (David Williamson). Order: full 1" spacer, back camber off toward -0.5°, check pressures; moving the Koni to the other frame hole changes nothing at the same ride height (edwardb). Track cars running 315s or 335s at -3.5° camber end up notching and re-welding the frame channel (Jphoenix, Rsnake). Rear IRS hubs ship with metric studs; the FFR 1/2-20 replacements are too long once a spacer is on, so P100DHG used shorter Dorman 610-364 studs. Use hubcentric spacers (jdavis500 went through a non-hubcentric set first; Amazon B01BEI808K hubcentric 1.25" was $45). edwardb: the coupe body is 72-5/8" at the rear wheel lips vs 70-3/8" on the roadster with the same IRS, which is why coupes run 1–1.125" spacers.

name: Flex-a-lite 16" LoBoy fan + Breeze shroud

users: Jphoenix Coupe-R (race: FFR fan "noisy and ineffective", temps fine after)
notes: Track data point: the stock FFR 16" fan was swapped out and the FFR radiator kept as a spare. On a street 347 the standard radiator and fan with the Breeze shroud is what most coupes run.

name: PSC quick-ratio power rack + Heidts valve + Jones pump (track)
model: PSC RA-33500 quick-ratio rack, Heidts control valve, Jones Racing pump with 6.5" pulley, PS fluid cooler
users: Jphoenix Coupe-R (after the Ford rack and GM Type 2 pump failed repeatedly); Rsnake (open-road winner, "much more precise")
notes: Track-only lesson: Ford racks and small-pulley pumps cook on a road course (Dave Tabor killed Ford OEM and KRC 4" pumps too; his fix was a KRC pump on a 6" pulley with an underdrive crank). A street car with the Breeze/Unisteer or ePowerSteering setup does not need this. ePowerSteering notes the FFR racks are 15:1.

name: Car Chemistry CC Inserts in the FFR side pipes
model: Car Chemistry CC Inserts / Classic Chambered baffles slid into the stock FFR side pipes; louvers face the exhaust flow; spiralturbobaffles.com is the alternative
users: tnt_motorsports (roadster: "takes the bark off the top end"); several in the Portland dB thread
notes: The cheapest way to pass a 102–103 dB track limit or quiet the cabin without new pipes. Angle the tips away from the pavement. Jphoenix runs standard FFR ROADSTER side pipes on his street Type 65 (302 + GAS-N headers) and is under the limit at every PNW track including Portland.
popWhy: Most common fix named in the Portland dB thread

name: 7" LED headlights that fit the FFR buckets
model: Holley RetroBright 7" round (PNWTim: drill the bucket ~13/16" for the pigtail) or Morimoto Sealed7 2.0 (JimStone)
users: PNWTim #620 (RetroBright); JimStone #576 (Morimoto Sealed7 2.0)
notes: The headlight-bucket cutouts FFR made in PNWTim's body were badly undersized: open them with a carbide burr before fitting the buckets. Period-correct look with LED output; wire to the Breeze or FFR harness like the stock lamps. Factory Five tech (Nov 10, 2026): the undersized headlight cutouts are intentional. Every body cutout is left small so you trim to a perfect fit; plan the burr work.

name: Hood hinge wedge (or FFR's revised hinges)
model: 3D-printed wedge, about 1/2" over 5-7/8" rise/run, under each hinge bracket (flight_83 prints them free for forum members); Todd Baumann at Build School cuts and re-welds the bracket instead; 2025 kits (Lugnut Mark #686) came with revised hinges needing no wedge
users: PNWTim #620; flight_83; Todd Baumann (FFR Build School); Lugnut Mark #686 got revised hinges
notes: The hood hinge brackets have had the wrong geometry since Gen 1 (edwardb's old thread). Measure yours: PNWTim's sat at ~83.5°, Indy Shu's at ~98°; if they lie flat you need nothing. Ask FFR for the revised hinges before fabricating; a 2029 kit should have them. Factory Five tech (Nov 10, 2026): the nose hinges were revised and the new ones are standard on every coupe now, under the same part number as the old ones, so there is no number to check at delivery. Measure the bracket angle anyway before fitting.

name: Used 3.73 Torsen center section (salvage) instead of FFR's
model: 2015+ Mustang GT 3.73 Torsen from LKQ or a salvage yard, checked by a diff shop; FFR credits the center section and you pay for the rest of the IRS kit
users: P100DHG #138 (LKQ, 27k mi, $385 + $20 check; paid FFR $450 for the remaining IRS parts); JimStone #576 (Georgia salvage, 17k mi); PNWTim #620 (used 2024 GT 3.73 after two new 3.55s leaked)
notes: 3.73 is the only ratio Ford sold as a Torsen for this housing and the Ford part (M-4001-88373T) is discontinued, so used is the normal route. A Torsen takes no friction modifier (Hoopers Rear End). Replace the half-shaft seals while it is out. Verify ratio and driveshaft length against the TKX before buying. Factory Five tech (Nov 10, 2026) confirms the catch: FFR only stocks the diff with the spindles and hubs as one assembly, so a salvage diff means sourcing spindles and hubs too (new from Ford, or from the same donor). Price that in before deleting.
